questions.q: What does Moses tell the people to always keep?
questions.a: He tells them to always keep Yahweh’s rules, statutes, decrees, and commandments.

questions.q: Who had not seen all that Yahweh did in Egypt?
questions.a: The children of the Israelites who were born while they wandered in the wilderness had not seen Yahweh’s discipline and his mighty deeds that he did in Egypt.

questions.q: How did Yahweh destroy the army of Egypt when they pursued after Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh caused the water of the Sea of Reeds to drown the army of Egypt as they pursued after Israel.
The Israelites had seen all the great works that Yahweh did.

questions.q: What will happen to the people if they keep all the commandments?
questions.a: If they keep all the commandments, they will be strong, go in and possess the land, and they and their descendants will live in the land for a long time.

questions.q: How is the land they are going to enter different from the land of Egypt?
questions.a: In the land they are going to enter there are many hills and valleys and plenty of water from the rain.

questions.q: What would Yahweh give them if they obey his commandments and to love and serve him with all their heart and soul?
questions.a: Yahweh will give them rain in its season, that they may gather their grain and be able to make wine and oil.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do if the people turn aside and worship other gods?
questions.a: He will become angry and will restrain the heavens so there will not be any rain.

questions.q: What should the people do so that they will live for a very long time in the land?
questions.a: They will write the commandments on the doorposts of their house and on their gates.

questions.q: If the people keep all the commandments of Yahweh and cling to him, what will he do for them?
questions.a: Yahweh will drive out all the other nations that are larger and mightier than they are.

questions.q: Why would no man be able to stand before Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh will cause the people of that land to fear and feel terror of Israel.

questions.q: What did Moses give Israel that day?
questions.a: He gave them a blessing and a curse.

questions.q: Where must the people go in order to possess the land?
questions.a: They must cross over the Jordan to possess and live in the land.

commentary.text: The great work God wrought for Israel.
Careful study of God's word requisite.
The blessings and the curse set forth.

Verses 1–7 Observe the connexion of these two; Thou shalt love the Lord, and keep his charge. Love will work in obedience, and that only is acceptable obedience which flows from a principle of love, 1Jo 5:3. Moses recounts some of the great and terrible works of God which their eyes had seen. What our eyes have seen, especially in our early days, should affect us, and make us better long afterwards.

Moses sets before them, for the future, life and death, the blessing and the curse, according as they did or did not keep God's commandment. Sin tends to shorten the days of all men, and to shorten the days of a people's prosperity. God will bless them with an abundance of all good things, if they would love him and serve him. Godliness has the promise of the life that now is; but the favour of God shall put gladness into the heart, more than the increase of corn, and wine, and oil. Revolt from God to idols would certainly be their ruin. Take heed that your hearts be not deceived. All who forsake God to set their affection upon any creature, will find themselves wretchedly deceived, to their own destruction; and this will make it worse, that it was for want of taking heed.

Let all be directed by the three rules here given. 1. Let our hearts be filled with the word of God. There will not be good practices in the life, unless there be good thoughts, good affections, and good principles in the heart. 2. Let our eyes be fixed upon the word of God, having constant regard to it as the guide of our way, as the rule of our work, Ps 119:30. 3. Let our tongues be employed about the word of God. Nor will any thing do more to cause prosperity, and keeping up religion in a nation, than the good education of children.

Moses sums up all the arguments for obedience in two words, the blessing and the curse. He charged the people to choose which they would have. Moses then appointed a public and solemn proclamation of the blessing and curse, to be made upon the two mountains of Gerizim and Ebal. We have broken the law, and are under its curse, without remedy from ourselves. In mercy, the gospel again sets before us a blessing and a curse. A blessing, if we obey the call to repentance, to faith in Christ, and newness of heart and life through him; an awful curse, if we neglect so great salvation. Let us thankfully welcome these glad tidings of great joy; and let us not harden our hearts, but hear this voice of God while it is called to-day, and while he invites us to come to him upon a mercy-seat. Let us be diligent to make our calling and election sure.
